claim: The phase 3 HERCULES trial reported that tolebrutinib reduced 6-month confirmed disability progression versus placebo in non-relapsing secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (22.6% versus 30.7%; hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.88), while liver-enzyme elevations were more frequent with tolebrutinib.
future_grounding_route: Obtain a longitudinal CNS-penetrant-BTK-inhibitor cohort with baseline and early-treatment blood or CSF, exposure, MRI, and confirmed-disability-progression outcomes; test frozen project modules without changing the V22 rule.

project_finding_reference.finding_id: No project-grounded progression treatment or biomarker

project_use: Current clinical context for choosing the most decision-relevant future progression-treatment cohort; it is not project-grounded support for a project module or target.
relationship_note: The trial establishes externally that a CNS-penetrant BTK-inhibitor strategy can affect disability progression in a defined SPMS population. It does not validate the project's APC/HLA-II, CD44/CXCR4, MIF, or lysosomal measurements.

source.citation: Fox RJ et al. Tolebrutinib in Nonrelapsing Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis. New England Journal of Medicine. 2025;392:1883-1892.
source.label: HERCULES phase 3 report

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: NEJM publication metadata and short paraphrase only
source_terms.reuse_notes: This record stores citation metadata and a short factual paraphrase; it does not redistribute article text.

why_unverifiable: The project does not hold participant-level HERCULES data and cannot rerun its efficacy or safety analyses.
